prompt.context: Our client, Bun on the Run, operates a fast food restaurant chain. The industry's average profit margin is 3 to 5%. However, our client currently is making only 1.5%.
prompt.question: How can you help them increase their margins to 3%?

clarifying_info.q: Where are the fast food outlets located?
clarifying_info.a: The outlets are on toll roads and in airports. The airport outlets are franchises.

clarifying_info.q: Which part of the business is driving the low margins?
clarifying_info.a: Airports constitute most of their business, and the low profit margins are due to the airport business.

clarifying_info.q: What is the state of the industry?
clarifying_info.a: The industry is fairly mature and stagnant.

clarifying_info.q: How large is the client's market presence?
clarifying_info.a: The client operates in 80% of airports and is present in all large airports, servicing 90% of all airport passengers.
There is only one other competitor, who has the remaining 10% market share; their margins are on par with the industry average.

clarifying_info.q: What does the menu look like?
clarifying_info.a: Standard fast food menu; the competitor's menu is no different.

clarifying_info.q: What does the cost structure look like?
clarifying_info.a: Variable costs are 70% of revenue (COGS: 35%, Labor: 35%). Fixed costs are 30% (Airport fee: 10%, Infrastructure: 5%, Rent: 15%).

Core ingredients (bread, meat, etc.) are 70% of COGS — already optimized and cannot be cut further. Non-core ingredients (paper towels, ketchup, etc.) are 30% of COGS, contracted through SYSCO at competitive rates.

clarifying_info.q: What does the labor situation look like?
clarifying_info.a: Most employees are salaried and full time, earning minimum wage of $6/hour. Benefits start after 6 months. Turnover is 200%. A new employee costs an additional $18/hour, which includes training (4 weeks) and a background check.

framework: Profitability lens: Revenue vs. Cost — since the industry is mature and the client has 90% market share, focus on costs
Break costs into variable (70%) and fixed (30%)
COGS already optimized; non-core contracted at competitive rates — limited cost-reduction opportunity
Labor: identify root cause of high labor costs — 200% annual turnover driving excessive new-hire expense
Fixed costs: airport fees, infrastructure, rent — likely contractual and difficult to change short-term
Root cause: high turnover means constant training spend ($18/hr additional cost per new hire) eroding margins

questions.prompt: Walk through the cost structure and identify where the margin problem is most likely coming from.
questions.guidance: A strong candidate systematically eliminates buckets. Revenue-side is hard to grow (90% market share, mature industry, standard menu, no pricing power). On costs: COGS is optimized, fixed costs are likely locked in by contracts. Labor at 35% of revenue with 200% turnover is the key lever. The $18/hr training cost on top of $6/hr wages means new hires cost 4x the steady-state wage rate during onboarding, which bleeds margins when turnover is this high.

math.setup: Estimate the cost drag from turnover. If average employee earns $6/hr and a new hire costs $18/hr in additional training/onboarding cost for 4 weeks of training: effective hourly cost during training = $6 + $18 = $24/hr. That is 4x the normal $6/hr wage rate. With 200% annual turnover, every position turns over twice per year, each time incurring 4 weeks of elevated cost.
steps: Normal annual labor cost per position: $6/hr x 40 hr/wk x 52 wk = ~$12,480
Additional training cost per hire: $18/hr x 40 hr/wk x 4 wk = $2,880
With 200% turnover, each position generates 2 new-hire events per year: 2 x $2,880 = $5,760 additional cost per position per year
Training cost as % of normal annual wage: $5,760 / $12,480 = ~46% premium on labor cost per position
math.answer: High turnover inflates effective labor cost by roughly 46% per position annually, significantly compressing margins.

brainstorming.prompt: What suggestions would you make to reduce employee turnover and increase retention at Bun on the Run?

categories.name: Compensation & Benefits
ideas: Pay above minimum wage to reduce incentive to leave for competitors like McDonalds
Make benefits available earlier than the current 6-month threshold to improve retention during the critical early tenure period
Introduce performance-based bonuses tied to retention milestones

categories.name: Career Development & Job Satisfaction
ideas: Cross-train employees across roles (cashier, prep, grill) to increase engagement and reduce monotony
Create a clear promotion path from crew to shift leader to manager
Offer skills certifications that have value beyond this employer

categories.name: Hiring & Onboarding
ideas: Improve screening to hire candidates more likely to stay long-term
Reduce the 4-week training period if possible through better onboarding materials or technology
Hire part-time or flexible-schedule workers who value flexibility over higher wages

categories.name: Work Environment
ideas: Improve scheduling flexibility to attract workers who value work-life balance
Conduct stay interviews to understand why employees are leaving
Create a better workplace culture in airport locations

recommendation: Root cause of the margin shortfall is a 200% annual employee turnover rate, which drives excessive training and onboarding costs on top of minimum-wage labor
Priority action: increase employee retention through a combination of earlier benefit eligibility and modest wage increases above minimum wage to close the gap with nearby competitors like McDonalds
Secondary action: implement cross-training to increase job satisfaction with minimal cost, while being mindful that cross-training may temporarily reduce utilization during the training period
risks: Raising wages increases the labor cost base; must model whether retention savings exceed the wage increase cost
Earlier benefits eligibility increases benefits expense; again requires cost-benefit analysis
Cross-training reduces utilization in the short term while employees learn new roles
next_steps: Quantify the exact turnover cost per location and compare against cost of proposed retention measures
Pilot a retention program (earlier benefits + slight wage premium) in 2-3 airports and measure turnover and margin impact
Assess whether any fixed cost components (airport fees, rent) have upcoming contract renewals that could be renegotiated
